newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault, Turkish partner reinforce links.
newsitem.headline: Renault, Turkish partner reinforce links.

text.p: French carmaker Renault and its Turkish partner Oyak plan to reinforce their links by increasing their cross-holdings in the industrial subsidiary Oyak-Renault and the marketing company MAIS, Renault said on Wednesday.

"As part of the strategy to consolidate Renault's position on a market with a strong growth potential..., Renault and its Turkish partner Oyak confirm their determination to strengthen their ties and seek greater cohesion between the brand's industrial and commercial activities, handled respectively by Oyak-Renault and MAIS," it said in a statement.
"To that end, both partners are to develop synergies and balance the level of their shareholdings in the two companies with a 51-49 split," it said.
Renault will boost its share of MAIS's equity to 49 percent from 20 percent, and Oyak will raise its stake in Oyak-Renault to 49 percent from 43 percent.
Officials at Renault declined to give financial details of the transaction.

Renault said in its statement that the two companies would strengthen their links to eliminate duplication, better integrate MAIS and Oyak-Renault into the Renault group operations and modernise the marketing facilities.
Oyak-Renault, formed in 1969, assembles Renault 12, 9 and 19 models in its plant at Bursa, which produced 66,960 vehicles in 1996. Renault currently holds 57 percent.
MAIS, which has six branch offices and 238 dealerships, sells vehicles assembled at Bursa and imports. Oyak now holds 80 percent.
Renault took 28.5 percent of the Turkish car market in 1996 with sales of 67,649 vehicles. Oyak-Renault exported 3,320 vehicles last year, mainly to Lebanon, Azerbaijan, Macedonia and Morocco.
